items.title: Age, Steatotic Liver Disease, Cardiometabolic Risks and Alcohol on Cardiorenal Outcomes and Mortality: Chinese Cohort.
items.abstract: Steatotic liver disease (SLD) is increasingly diagnosed in younger adults, yet whether its long-term risk profiles differ by age remains poorly defined. Within the prospective Kailuan cohort, 34,988 participants with incident SLD were identified and matched (up to 1:4) with the non-SLD controls. Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs), while eXtreme Gradient Boosting with SHapley Additive exPlanations quantified the relative importance of SLD, cardiometabolic risk factors (CMRFs), and alcohol on chronic kidney disease (CKD), cardiovascular disease (CVD), and mortality across age groups. After a median follow-up of >10 years, the HRs for the associations between SLD and CKD (HR: 1.44, 95% CI: 1.22-1.70), CVD (1.65, 1.23-2.23), and mortality (1.46, 1.05-2.03) were significantly stronger in the early-onset (≤40 years) group than in late-onset (>40 years) group (all P for interaction <0.05). Alcohol-related subtypes exhibited a positive dose-response for CKD only in the early-onset group. SHAP analysis within models restricted to the predefined domains (SLD, CMRFs and alcohol) suggested that SLD had relatively high predictive importance for adverse outcomes in early-onset group, whereas the predictive importance of CMRFs predominated in late-onset group. Age significantly modifies the associations of SLD, CMRFs, and alcohol with clinical outcomes. The relative impact of SLD on cardiorenal risk is most pronounced in early adulthood, supporting the potential value of age-tailored risk assessment, though interventional validation is needed.

items.title: Exploring Patients' Perception of Integrating an AI-Powered Clinical Intelligence Companion in a Resource-Constrained Setting: A Cross-Sectional Multi-Centre Study.
items.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI)-powered conversational agents into healthcare has steadily progressed towards real-world deployment, despite limited patient-level evidence regarding acceptability in low-resource settings. This study assessed patients' perceptions, acceptance, and concerns regarding the use of an AI-powered Clinical Intelligence Companion-Hami® in outpatient clinics of a resource-constrained setting. A cross-sectional study was conducted at four hospitals in Karachi, Pakistan. A structured survey comprising demographic information and nine questions to assess perceptions was completed by 8,487 patients after they interacted with Hami®. Frequencies and percentages were reported for all responses. Binary logistic regression was performed to explore factors associated with patients' acceptance followed by a sensitivity analysis excluding 'Unsure' responses and a post-hoc Benjamini-Hochberg test. Adjusted Odds Ratios (aORs) with 95% Confidence Intervals (CIs) from the primary analysis were considered for estimates that were significant in both analyses. Patients were receptive to Hami®'s integration into healthcare settings (79.7%) and found its questioning relevant (92.3%) and language appropriate (95.7%), with lower concerns (7.7% to 13.7%). Patients aged 18-44 years reported higher odds of agreement with Hami®'s relevant questioning (aOR 1.33; 95% CI: 1.04 - 1.70) and younger and middle-aged patients had lower odds of concerns as compared to older adults (>65 years). In contrast to uneducated patients, educated patients were less likely to support integration (aOR 0.84; 95% CI: 0.75 - 0.94) and had nearly two times higher odds of concerns regarding reduced contact with providers (aOR 1.91; 95% CI: 1.64 - 2.21) and decreased human aspects of care (aOR 2.10; 95% CI: 1.81 - 2.43) using Hami®. Patients attending participating private hospitals had lowers odds of agreement with the relevance of Hami®'s questioning (aOR 0.66; 95% CI: 0.51 - 0.85) and highest odds of concerns regarding confidentiality breaches (aOR 2.11; 95% CI: 1.57 - 2.82), decreased human aspects of care (aOR 2.07; 95% CI: 1.65 - 2.61) and unclear accountability (aOR 2.05; 95% CI: 1.58 - 2.65) as compared to patients attending participating public hospital. Integrating Hami® in a resource-constrained setting reveals differential readiness for AI-assisted care, with higher acceptance among younger patients, fewer concerns among both younger and middle-aged patients, and higher concerns among educated patients and those visiting participating private hospitals. These findings underscore that patients' socio-demographics are potentially associated with digital health acceptance and that implementation strategies should address group-specific concerns. However, these differences may reflect case-mix, workflow, or digital infrastructure across participating sites as well as patients' health and digital literacy. By prioritizing transparent communication regarding data privacy and confidentiality, ensuring clinician oversight, and positioning AI as a supportive tool that preserves essential human interaction, patients' concerns can be mitigated.

items.title: Acute Ischemic Stroke Cases with a Rare Etiology: Free-Floating Thrombus (FFT); Experiences of a Single Centre.
items.abstract: Free-floating thrombus (FFT) is a rare and clinically critical imaging finding in acute ischemic stroke associated with a high embolic risk. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical, radiological, etiological, and therapeutic characteristics, as well as outcomes, of patients presenting with acute ischemic stroke and FFT. This retrospective single-center series included patients evaluated for acute ischemic stroke between 2021 and 2025 who met the study's FFT criteria on vascular imaging. Diagnosis used dynamic Doppler confirmation in accessible extracranial arteries and computed tomography angiography (CTA) morphology in anatomically inaccessible segments. Clinical presentation, etiology according to the Trial of Org 10172 in Acute Stroke Treatment (TOAST) classification, antithrombotic treatment, vascular outcomes, and 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) scores were described. Clinical and imaging follow-up extended to at least 6 months in surviving patients. Among 2150 patients with comprehensive vascular imaging, 31 (1.4%) met the FFT criteria (mean age, 61.4 ± 16.0 years; 54.8% female). The internal carotid artery was the most frequent location (25/31; 80.6%). TOAST categories were undetermined etiology in 17 patients (54.8%), cardioembolism in seven (22.6%), large-artery atherosclerosis in five (16.1%), and other determined etiologies in two (6.5%). The undetermined group comprised 15 patients without an identified cause and two with competing mechanisms. All patients initially received anticoagulation. Complete and partial recanalization were observed in 17 (54.8%) and 12 (38.7%) patients, respectively. Seven patients underwent carotid revascularization after thrombus stabilization, with no residual stenosis and no procedure-related complications within 30 days. At 90 days, 28 patients (90.3%) had mRS scores of 0-2. FFT is a morphological finding occurring across different stroke mechanisms. This series describes imaging-based assessment, initial anticoagulation, and subsequent carotid revascularization in selected patients. Its uncontrolled, descriptive design does not establish treatment efficacy, an optimal anticoagulation duration, or the preferred timing of intervention.

items.title: Cardiac Structure and Function in Migraine and Tension-Type Headache. A HUNT Population-Based Study.
items.abstract: To evaluate whether primary headache disorders, especially migraine and tension-type headache (TTH), are associated with alterations in cardiac structure and function. We analyzed data from the HUNT4 survey (2017-2019), a population-based cohort study in Norway. Of 5752 individuals aged ≥ 20 years randomly selected for echocardiographic evaluation of cardiac structure and function, 2039 (35%) participants with complete headache and echocardiographic data were included. Individuals with prior stroke, myocardial infarction, or heart failure were excluded. Headache types were classified using validated questionnaires. Associations were analyzed using adjusted linear regression models. Among 2039 participants, the majority were women and under the age of 65 years. Compared to those without headache, individuals with migraine (n = 150) and TTH (n = 286) had 4%-15% and 4%-8% smaller cardiac volumes, respectively. However, after adjustment for potential confounders, only TTH was associated with a significantly lower left ventricle end-diastolic volume with β-coefficients of -4.04 mL (95% CI, -6.87 to -1.20), whereas no significant differences were observed for migraine (-2.62, 95% CI, -7.01 to 1.76) or unclassified headaches (-1.29, 95% CI -5.23 to 2.63). Diastolic early mitral inflow velocity (E-wave) was significantly lower in individuals with migraine with aura (-4.80 cm/s, 95% CI -8.50, -1.11). Our findings suggest a potential association between TTH and subclinical changes in left ventricular volumes. Migraine with aura showed modest reductions in mitral E-wave velocity, without evidence of cardiac dysfunction. Further studies are needed to confirm these observations and explore their clinical relevance.

items.title: Association of the Geriatric Nutritional Risk Index with Cognitive Function Level and Cognitive Impairment among Older Adults with Cardiometabolic Disease.
items.abstract: This study aimed to assess the association of Geriatric Nutritional Risk Index (GNRI) with cognitive function level and cognitive impairment risk among older adults with cardiometabolic disease using data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES). Using cross-sectional data from the NHANES, this research included 1,937 participants aged 60 years or older with at least one cardiometabolic disease (diabetes, hypertension, stroke, or congestive heart failure). Cognitive function was assessed using the CERAD tests, Animal Fluency Test (AFT), and Digit Symbol Substitution Test (DSST). Multivariable linear and logistic regression analyses were used to estimate the β coefficients and odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for the associations of GNRI with cognitive function level and risk of cognitive impairment. A total of 1937 participants aged≥60 years with cardiometabolic disease were included. The results showed that per 1-SD increase in GNRI was associated with increased cognitive function levels, including CERAD: Trial 1 (β=0.11, 95% CI: 0.03-0.19), CERAD: Trial 3 (β=0.12, 95% CI: 0.04-0.21), CERAD: Delayed Recall (β=0.21, 95% CI: 0.11-0.32), CERAD test (β=0.53, 95% CI: 0.23-0.82), and AFT (β=0.34, 95% CI: 0.11-0.57) scores. Restricted cubic splines showed significantly positive linear dose-response associations between GNRI and cognitive function. Compared to participants with the lowest quartile (Q1) of GNRI, those with the highest quartile (Q4) had a lower cognitive impairment risk (OR=0.59, 95% CI: 0.41-0.85). Potential mechanisms underlying GNRI's protective effect against cognitive impairment may involve the pleiotropic neuroprotection of albumin and body mass index-mediated brain structural changes. Higher GNRI is independently associated with better cognitive function and reduced risk of cognitive impairment in older adults with cardiometabolic diseases. To mitigate cognitive risk, implementing GNRI screening may identify high-risk older adults with cognitive impairment, prompting timely nutritional support that improves cognitive health and disease management.

items.title: Paired Deep Mutational Scanning of Lck Activity and Inhibitor Sensitivity Enables the Engineering of Pharmacological Control of T Cell Receptor Signaling.
items.abstract: Controlling signaling enzymes with small molecules is a central goal in chemical biology and is of great utility for engineering cell-derived immunotherapies. Yet strategies for conferring selective small-molecule sensitivity without disrupting a protein's native function remain limited. Here we present a generalizable approach to engineering small molecule-controlled multidomain protein kinases. Using deep mutational scanning of full-length Lck, a tyrosine kinase essential for T cell receptor (TCR) signaling, we measured the effect of nearly all single amino acid substitutions in the kinase domain on phosphotransferase activity. The resulting activity landscape defined the domain's tolerance to substitution, mapped the regulatory interfaces that tune phosphotransferase activity, and, by treating bulky substitutions as ligand proxies, nominated cryptic pockets where covalent liganding is predicted to allosterically inhibit Lck. In parallel screens, we measured the sensitization of each variant to five clinically approved, reversible drugs: dabrafenib, erlotinib, gefitinib, imatinib, and nilotinib. Together, these landscapes identified substitutions that preserved or enhanced activity while sensitizing Lck to inhibition. Sensitizing substitutions were distributed throughout the kinase domain, including positions more than 30 Å from the ATP-binding site, implicating long-range allosteric networks linking distal perturbations to ATP-binding site conformation and inhibitor potency. Integrating the activity and sensitization landscapes yielded a nilotinib-sensitized variant, I312S, that supports TCR signaling and, upon drug treatment, selectively suppresses proximal signaling and IL-2 production in Jurkat cells even in the presence of endogenous Lck.
items.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

items.title: High-Resolution Spatial Transcriptomics Reveals Millimeter-Scale Malignant Territories and Immune Exclusion patterns in Human Salivary Gland Adenoid Cystic Carcinoma.
items.abstract: Adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC) of the salivary gland (SGACC) is a rare malignancy with frequent late recurrence and limited response to systemic and immune therapies. Bulk and single-cell sequencing do not preserve tissue architecture, so the spatial organization of its MYB-driven myoepithelial and luminal tumor cells, stroma, and immune cells remains poorly defined. This study aimed to map the SGACC tumor microenvironment at near-cellular resolution. Visium HD based spatial transcriptomics was performed on four SGACC tissue sections from three patients with tubulo-cribriform tumor form in stage III - IV. Bins of 10 x 10 µm were annotated and deconvolved with cell2location using an integrated single-cell reference of 119,189 cells from 20 donors. Pseudobulk differential expression, spatial autocorrelation, potency and spatial trajectory inference, permutation-based territory analysis, Hotspot module detection, and marker-based immune profiling were applied. MYB-expressing luminal (LECs-MYB) and myoepithelial (MECs-MYB) epithelial cells occupied 55.7% of bins on average. The MECs-MYB to LECs-MYB ratio increased from the nest interior toward the tumor edge, where cancer-associated fibroblasts rose sharply. Potency and trajectory analyses placed MECs-MYB upstream of LECs-MYB. Malignant states formed territories of up to 38.0 mm² that persisted over 1.5 mm in three sections and contained spatially restricted programs. Hypoxic stressed territories also showed mTORC1, unfolded protein response, and cell-cycle programs. T/NK, myeloid, MHC class I and II, and plasma cell signatures were 1.4-to 5.7-fold higher in stroma than in tumor nests, whereas VTCN1 (B7-H4) was the only B7 family ligand enriched within nests. SGACC shows an ordered arrangement of malignant lineages, millimeter-scale malignant territories, MHC class - I and II enriched stroma, and immune-excluded nests enriched for B7-H4. These features provide evidence to be validated in larger cohorts with protein-level and clinical data. Adenoid cystic carcinoma is a rare cancer of the salivary glands that often returns years after treatment and responds poorly to current drugs and immunotherapy. Most earlier studies broke the tumor apart before measuring gene activity, losing the localization of cell in tumor. In this study, we measured gene activity directly on four thin tissue slices from the tumors of three patients at near single-cell detail. The two main types of cancer cells were arranged in an ordered pattern within tumor clusters, and cancer cells of the same type formed large regions several square millimeters in size, each with its own local gene activity. Immune cell signals stayed mostly in the surrounding supportive tissue and rarely reached the tumor clusters, while the tumor cells showed high activity of the gene for B7-H4 that can dampen immune responses. The patient with the longest recorded survival had an altered territory make up from that of other patients that points towards features that studies with larger cohort size can test and develop targeted treatment approaches.

items.title: Development of Novel NPC1-Targeting Autophagy Inhibitors for the Treatment of Uveal Melanoma.
items.abstract: Uveal melanoma (UM) is the most common primary intraocular malignancy in adults, and up to 50% of patients develop liver metastases. Metastatic UM responds poorly to conventional chemotherapy and currently available immunotherapies, highlighting the need for new therapeutic strategies. Because UM cells rely on lysosome-dependent stress-response pathways, including autophagy, we evaluated previously reported betulinic acid (BetA) derivatives and identified ALS-997 as a potent inhibitor of autophagic flux in UM cells. The anticancer activity of BetA derivatives was evaluated using the NCI-60 cancer cell line panel and WST-1 viability assays in UM cell lines and normal human melanocytes. Effects on autophagy and lysosomal function were assessed by western blotting for mTOR and autophagy associated proteins, LysoTracker Green imaging, and filipin III/LAMP2 staining. Apoptosis was evaluated by PARP cleavage and caspase-3 cleavage. The interaction of ALS-997 with Niemann-Pick disease type C1 (NPC1) was examined using a cellular thermal shift assay and computational molecular docking. NPC1 expression in UM cells and normal melanocytes was compared by quatitative PCR and western blotting. ALS-997 preferentially reduced the viability of UM cell relative to normal melanocytes. Treatment with ALS-997 disrupted autophagic flux and lysosomal function, induced lysosomal cholesterol accumulation, and activated apoptotic signaling. ALS-997 also altered the thermal stability of NPC1, supporting cellular target engagement, while molecular docking predicted a direct interaction between ALS-997 and NPC1. NPC1 expression was higher in UM cells than in normal melanocytes. ALS-997 is a BetA-derived compound that disrupts lysosomal cholesterol homeostasis and autophagic flux, leading to apoptosis in UM cells. These findings support NPC1 as a potential therapeutic target in UM.

items.title: Computational modeling of breast cancer metastases predicts response to dual checkpoint inhibition and reveals spatially-informed treatments.
items.abstract: In advanced breast cancers, the highly suppressive tumor microenvironment contributes to poor responses to immune checkpoint inhibition. The degree of suppression varies by site of disease and affects metastatic progression. To investigate this phenomenon, we developed an agent-based model of cell-cell interactions within the tumor microenvironment, specifically tuned to in vivo data from murine breast-to-lung metastases. The model includes nine functional cell types (cancer cells, M0-, M1-, and M2-like macrophages, CD4+ T cells, T regulatory cells [Tregs], CD8+ T cells, NK cells, and MDSC-like cells). We incorporated a novel continuum model to describe exhaustion of CD8+ T and NK cells, where exhaustion is impacted by cell-cell interactions in the TME. We also modeled the effect of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI) anti-PD-1 and anti-CTLA-4, termed "dual ICIs". We used this model to simulate the spatiotemporal trajectories of 19 metastases without treatment and with dual ICIs. The model predicted that dual ICIs lead to statistically significant reductions in cancer cell proliferation in seven of the metastases (37%), and spatial analyses of these metastases reveal structural similarities at multiple scales of tumor organization. Additionally, spatial analysis suggests that high colocalization of CD8+ T cells with Tregs could prevent dual ICIs from being effective, and simulation of Treg blockade combined with dual ICIs led to 15 total metastases having a statistically significant treatment effect (80% total). Our model provides a highly resolved spatiotemporal platform for studying cell-cell interactions that drive resistance to ICIs and identifies potential therapeutic avenues to enhance the efficacy of immunotherapies.

items.title: Optimizing early and locally advanced NSCLC: A Portuguese expert consensus on treatment pathways.
items.abstract: Management of early and locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is increasingly complex due to expanding therapeutic options, requiring integration of efficacy, safety, and quality of life. As treatment options continue to evolve, structured, multidisciplinary approaches are essential. This study aims to develop tailored treatment algorithms and clinical recommendations for early and locally advanced NSCLC in Portugal. These recommendations will continue to evolve as the treatment landscape expands. A multidisciplinary panel of 12 experts (4 pulmonologists/oncologists, 4 thoracic surgeons, 4 radiation oncologists) participated in a structured Patient Profile Think Tank. Current diagnostic, staging, and treatment strategies for early and locally advanced NSCLC were reviewed. Consensus statements were generated through iterative discussions and validated via voting. Key decision points were integrated into treatment algorithms, supported by literature. Consensus was reached on several key treatment decision points, including mandatory molecular testing at initial diagnosis and re-evaluation; standardised criteria for tumour resectability; and the integration of immunotherapy and targeted therapies in NSCLC. Multidisciplinary team discussions were considered essential throughout the patient pathway. This initiative provides the first Portuguese expert consensus on early and locally advanced NSCLC, offering evidence-based recommendations and practical algorithms to standardise care and improve outcomes, while adapting international evidence to the national context. Future efforts should focus on digital clinical implementation and extending approaches to metastatic disease.

items.title: Modeling spontaneous hepatitis C virus clearance by age, sex, IFNL4 genotype, and infection history: Implications for simulations of elimination and vaccine trials.
items.abstract: The probability of hepatitis C virus (HCV) clearance is mediated by an interaction between numerous factors. However, variation in spontaneous HCV clearance was previously modeled using relatively simple approaches with fixed probabilities by sex. Here, we developed a literature-informed clearance algorithm that considers age, sex, interferon lambda 4 ( IFNL4 ) genotype, and infection history to model the probability of HCV clearance in vulnerable populations, such as people who inject drugs (PWID), and in controlled human infection (CHI) models for future HCV vaccines. We modeled HCV clearance probabilities for three infection-history pathways: first infection, reinfection after spontaneous clearance, and reinfection after direct-acting antiviral (DAA) cure. Logistic and cumulative-hazard equations assigned person-specific clearance probabilities in the first two pathways. The post-DAA pathway used fixed clearance probabilities. We tested the algorithm using HepCEP (Hepatitis C Elimination in PWID), an agent-based simulator. First-infection clearance probabilities ranged from 0.13 to 0.51 across eight age, sex, and IFNL4 genotype subgroups. Clearance probabilities for reinfection after spontaneous clearance ranged from 0.20 to 0.80 at literature point estimates. Across 100 runs, the mean assigned clearance probabilities were 0.27 for first infections and 0.52 for reinfections after spontaneous clearance, compared with literature inputs of 0.26 and 0.52, respectively. Probabilities varied across subgroups and runs. Simulations reproduced the algorithm's intended clearance heterogeneity and uncertainty by age, sex, IFNL4 genotype, and infection history, which may support models of HCV elimination in vulnerable populations and CHI model development for future HCV vaccines.
items.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences

items.title: Global and National Perspectives on the Role of the WHO Model Lists of Essential Medicines.
items.abstract: Since 1977, the World Health Organization (WHO) Model Lists of Essential Medicines (EML) have guided countries in selecting medicines that address priority health needs. This study explores how global and national stakeholders interpret the role of the WHO EML and why its impact on access varies across therapeutic areas. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 52 participants across 17 countries. Data were analyzed thematically and mapped onto a two-axis framework reflecting trust in EML as a selection reference and control over access policies. Findings reveal that the influence of the EML was greatest where inclusion aligned with financing and procurement mechanisms, as seen in HIV and hepatitis C, where pooled procurement and voluntary licensing (and compulsory licensing as in the case of hepatitis C medicines) translated listing into tangible access gains. In contrast, in high-priced therapeutic areas, EML inclusion was often described as aspirational, reflecting clinical priority without resolving affordability or implementation barriers. In many national settings, the EML substitutes for formal health technology assessment but remains weakly connected to reimbursement and procurement decisions. Overall, the study indicates that the influence of the WHO EML depends on whether its normative authority is linked to concrete mechanisms that enable affordability and access.
items.journal: The Journal of law, medicine & ethics : a journal of the American Society of Law, Medicine & Ethics

items.title: Trend analysis from 1990 to 2020 reveals a decline in hepatocellular carcinoma in Osaka, Japan.
items.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality. In Japan, the historically high HCC burden has been largely driven by hepatitis virus infection, although metabolic and lifestyle-related risk factors have become increasingly prevalent. This study describes long-term trends in HCC incidence in Osaka Prefecture from 1990 to 2020. Population-based data from the Osaka Cancer Registry were used to identify newly diagnosed HCC cases, defined as International Classification of Diseases for Oncology, Third Edition, topography code C22.0 with morphology codes 8170-8175 and behavior code 3. Sex-specific and age-standardized incidence rates were calculated using the World Health Organization 2000-2025 world standard population. Age-specific rates were estimated for individuals aged 50-79 years, and temporal trends were evaluated using Joinpoint regression. From 1990 to 2020, 99,889 HCC patients were registered, of whom 70,962 (71.04%) were men and 28,927 (28.96%) were women. The age-standardized incidence rate declined from 45.77 to 14.56 per 100,000 persons in men and from 10.87 to 3.90 per 100,000 persons in women. Joinpoint analysis showed significant declines from 1997 onward in men and from 2000 onward in women. Age-specific incidence rates among individuals aged 50-79 years showed overall declines in both sexes, although the timing and magnitude varied by age and sex. Age-standardized HCC incidence rates in Osaka Prefecture declined substantially from 1990 to 2020 in both sexes, with distinct temporal patterns by age and sex. These findings provide a basis for understanding long-term changes in HCC incidence and informing prevention strategies.

items.title: Sex Differences in Liver Disease: From Biological Mechanisms to Clinical Translation.
items.abstract: Sex differences in liver disease are evident in epidemiology, pathophysiology, and clinical outcomes, although their magnitude and direction vary according to etiology, age, reproductive stage, exposure, and region. Men bear a higher global burden of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), whereas primary biliary cholangitis and autoimmune hepatitis predominantly affect women. These patterns reflect the interplay of hormonal, genetic, immunological, metabolic, behavioral, and social determinants. Women generally exhibit stronger innate and adaptive immune responses, which may promote viral clearance but also contribute to autoimmune susceptibility. Experimental studies have identified estrogen receptor, androgen receptor, and sex-chromosome-related pathways that may influence steatosis, fibrosis, and hepatocarcinogenesis. However, many proposed mechanisms remain incompletely validated in humans. Sex also influences pharmacokinetics and access to liver transplantation, whereas evidence for sex-specific differences in treatment efficacy, particularly in immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy for HCC, remains inconclusive. This review synthesizes evidence across major liver diseases with explicit evidence labels, separates biological sex from gender-related factors, and concludes that sex currently informs risk assessment, surveillance, and equitable care rather than sex-specific treatment.

items.title: Chemical Profiling of Wuwei Xiaodu Decoction and Its Plasma Constituents With Computational Assessment of Hepatitis-Related Targets.
items.abstract: Wuwei Xiaodu Decoction (WXD) has reported anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and immunomodulatory activities. Its constituents detectable in plasma after oral dosing are incompletely characterized. This study profiled WXD and its plasma constituents and used the latter to prioritize hepatitis-related targets computationally. The aqueous extract and pooled plasma collected from healthy mice 1 h after the final oral dose were profiled using ultra-performance liquid chromatography coupled to heated electrospray ionization high-resolution tandem mass spectrometry on a Q Exactive Plus platform. Post-dose plasma was compared with blank plasma, and assignments were confirmed against reference standards. Plasma-detected constituents were examined by network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics. The extract contained 77 identified or tentatively characterized compounds; standards confirmed 15 unchanged constituents in post-dose plasma. Their 294 predicted targets overlapped with 110 of 2063 hepatitis-related targets. Rutin-PTGS2 ranked first among 48 docking pairs (-10.796 kcal·mol -1 ). During a 100-ns simulation, rutin remained in contact with PTGS2, and structural fluctuations decreased in the later stage. This study characterized the WXD aqueous extract and confirmed 15 unchanged constituents in pooled plasma from healthy mice. Computational analysis of these constituents identified shared hepatitis-related targets, highlighted enriched pathways, and prioritized rutin-PTGS2 among the evaluated constituent-target pairs.
items.journal: Rapid communications in mass spectrometry : RCM

items.title: Learning spatial cellular state through 3D reconstruction of the cell.
items.abstract: Subcellular-resolution spatial transcriptomics localizes individual RNA transcripts within cells with high-precision. Existing methods for identifying spatially organized cell populations rely on cellular niches defined by neighboring cells, leaving open whether such populations can be identified from individual-cell representations alone. Moreover, representations that jointly capture transcript identity and three-dimensional (3D) spatial organization have not been systematically learned or biologically evaluated. Here we present a representation learning framework that models each cell as a gene-annotated point cloud of transcripts and trains a rotation-equivariant neural network to reconstruct 3D cell shape, yielding spatially informed transcript embeddings. We further aggregate these embeddings into a cell-state representation that summarizes transcript-level spatial patterns. Our framework outperforms existing point-cloud-based 3D reconstruction methods on cell-shape reconstruction. In MERFISH human uterine cancer, combining the learned embeddings with gene expression improved prediction of CD45RO protein intensity over both gene expression alone and niche-based embeddings. Applied to MERFISH human liver cancer and Xenium human lung datasets, our framework identified distinct spatial patterns between cell populations, including spatially organized subpopulations marked by disease-associated gene expression and patterns associated with pathological tissue structures. Together, these results show that learning transcript representations through 3D cell reconstruction provides a novel approach to capture cell-state heterogeneity and biologically relevant spatial organization in subcellular spatial transcriptomics.
items.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

items.title: Integrating locoregional and systemic approaches in advanced HCC.
items.abstract: The management of advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC; BCLC stage C) is undergoing a major paradigm shift. Although the Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer (BCLC) staging system has long provided clear sequential treatment algorithms, its rigid "systemic therapy only" recommendation for BCLC stage C fails to reflect the clinical and molecular heterogeneity of this population. In the era of immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-based systemic regimens, a single stage-based strategy is no longer sufficient. Because direct baseline measurement of tumor biology remains unfeasible in daily practice, dynamic treatment response could be a clinical marker of favorable tumor biology. Patients responding to systemic therapy likely possess more controllable tumor biology, which may offer a strategic opportunity to evaluate multimodal escalation-such as locoregional treatment, surgical conversion, or liver transplantation. Conversely, localized oligo-progression reflects focal escape rather than global failure, warranting targeted locoregional intervention while maintaining the effective ICI-based systemic backbone. For patients with poly-progression, tailored strategies based on disease patterns-such as regional modalities for liver-dominant progression-could be evaluated before routinely shifting to next-line systemic therapy. Successful implementation of this strategy requires a structured protocol considering treatment response, liver reserve, performance status, and anatomical feasibility, governed by a multidisciplinary team. Moving beyond rigid algorithms toward response-based selection could be a meaningful step toward optimizing personalized care for advanced HCC.

items.title: Resveratrol-loaded PLGA-microparticles induced apoptosis and inhibited migration capacity of 3D model of hepatocellular carcinoma.
items.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the most prevalent primary malignant liver tumor and remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. Developing effective therapeutic strategies for this life-threatening disease is of paramount importance. Resveratrol (RSV), a natural polyphenol, exhibits promising antitumor activity through the induction of apoptosis and inhibition of cancer cell proliferation. However, its clinical application is hindered by poor bioavailability and rapid metabolic inactivation. In this study, biodegradable poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) microparticles (MPs) were employed as a delivery vehicle to achieve controlled release of RSV within a liver cancer microtissue (LCMT) model. RSV-loaded MPs (RSV-MP) were prepared via a standard oil-in-water emulsion technique and characterized extensively. The RSV-MPs were incorporated into LCMTs composed of a co-culture of Huh-7 HCC cells and human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) at a 4:1 ratio, utilizing AggrewellTM plates. The anti-tumor efficacy of the RSV-MP drug delivery system was evaluated and compared with free RSV solution. Assays including Live/Dead assay, MTS proliferation, migration, and analyses of gene and protein expression were performed. Results demonstrated that the MP-mediated formulation significantly reduced cell viability more than free RSV (37.49% vs 56.14%, p** < 0.01). Moreover, the expression levels of apoptotic genes-BAX (p* ≤ 0.05), CASP3 (p*** ≤ 0.001), and TP53 (p** ≤ 0.01)-were markedly modulated following treatment. Western blot analysis corroborated these findings, revealing increased expression of cleaved-caspase-3 (p*** ≤ 0.001) and p53 protein (p** ≤ 0.01) in the RSV-MP group relative to free RSV. Migration assays further demonstrated a significant decrease in cell motility following MP treatment (p** ≤ 0.01). These findings suggest that RSV-loaded PLGA microparticles substantially enhance the anti-tumor efficacy of RSV in a physiologically relevant LCMT model. This delivery system warrants further investigation as a potential therapeutic approach for HCC.
